section_map.summary: Treaty only in principle. NDI, K-means, GEI. Two funders compared by fuzzy evaluation.
Virgin land, quoted treaty, question list, our work as bullets
Assumptions in three blocks. Symbol table is row-shifted.
Five aspects, entropy weights, three clusters, GEI 14.06, EU check
Economic, civilization, and industry rules, each with an aim sentence
Variance of five indicators. Only military weight falls.
Four strengths, two weaknesses, one-paragraph conclusion

contributions.summary: GEI is the relative gap between mean High and mean Low NDI, not a Gini or a Theil index. 2020 value 14.06.
EU REI falls from 2.65 in 1990 to 0.90 in 2015, with only two countries switching groups.
Four impact scores: state 2.332 and 2.312, private 2.003 and 1.708.
Every policy sentence is paired with an aim sentence.

dependency_graph.handoff: Entropy weights and the High or Low classification are the factor weights and the two groups of the fuzzy evaluation

assumptions.summary: International-organization data are accurate and mutually consistent.
Dropped countries barely move the weights.
A country is one unit. Relative and per-capita measures, not totals. Cultural influence excluded.
Development classes stay fixed. Mining is high-threshold. No single-government projects. No sudden change.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: 115 countries, 2016-2020, World Bank and UNdata. Countries with too many gaps dropped. Tolerable gaps filled by nearby-year average or a similar country.

models.summary: NDI: logic tree, entropy weights, K-means, GEI as a high-low ratio gap.
FCE: same weights, hand-set memberships, four impact scores.

verification.summary: Income gap of about ten times between K-means groups. COVID-19: poor countries' income falls about 3 percent, rich countries resist.
EU REI 2.65 to 0.90 over 25 years, called a logical tendency.
Raising variance raises four weights and lowers the military weight.

results_trace.summary: Capital formation 25.40 percent, income per capita 15.57 percent, R&D 15.81 percent. Grouped: economy 44.85, civilization 25.92, society 12.08, politics 10.00, environment 7.15.
2020 clusters: 29 high, 39 medium, 47 low. High mean NDI 11249, low mean 747. GEI 14.06.
State-funded impact 2.332 and 2.312. Private 2.003 and 1.708. State gap smaller.

writing_logic.summary: Summary is three blocks: measure, compare two conditions, test. Sequence words do the outlining: first, after that, then, finally.
Each indicator gets a belief sentence of the form 'we believe that the more X, the worse or better Y'. The tree is argued one leaf at a time.
The fuzzy section is a repeated stencil: mechanism, limit, grade. Indicators with no story are bundled as 'we don't think it has much to do with those'.
Policy is rule then aim. The aim sentence starts 'The policy aims to' or 'This policy is designed to'.

language_observations.summary: 'a virgin land for resource development' — one metaphor, then the treaty quotation. The metaphor is not repeated.
A string of real questions: technically feasible, who benefits, who leads, will the gap grow. The questions are the restatement.
A four-link comparative chain from out-of-pocket spending to class dropping.
Maslow's second layer recruited to justify military spending. One sentence, then the belief.
'It is worth mentioning' concedes no growth-rate gap, then COVID-19 supplies the difference the concession removed.
'making the rich richer, having little impact on the others' — the mechanism in eight words.
'counted as a partner, instead of just an employee, that is to say' — a status word, then the operational meaning.
'need to wait for the verification of future practice' — the honest limit of a scoring model with no mining data.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: A gap between the top and bottom clusters is easier to argue than a whole-distribution index, and the EU panel gives it a history.
Four numbers and two inequalities do the policy work: state funding helps both and widens less.
Each rule is followed by what it is for. A judge can reject the rule without losing the aim, or the reverse.

weaknesses.summary: Authors: missing data in some countries hurts the global result.
Authors: mining impacts are not yet observable, so the fuzzy scores wait on future practice.
Entropy interpretation is reversed relative to the standard method, and the membership degrees are stipulated.

independent_extensions.summary: Replace the stipulated 0.7 and 0.3 with a small elicited panel and report disagreement.
Reconcile the 'hundreds of times' sentence with the table, which shows a ratio near 15.

candidate_rule_impacts.summary: Inequity measured as a relative gap between extreme clusters, checked on a regional panel.
Policies grouped by the two heaviest indicator blocks, each rule paired with an aim.

unresolved_questions.question: Did the authors implement the standard entropy weight, or the reversed version their prose describes?
Can the four impact scores be recomputed from the garbled membership matrices?
